islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

turns.hypothesis: Meals come mostly from exploration, but every frontier mark is worth the same 0.12, so a crack between two walls pulls as hard as the edge of a big unexplored plain. A leaky blur of the unknown (`vast`) weights each frontier mark by how much unexplored space lies behind it (information gain), on top of confinement suppression; the agent should open new ground faster and waste fewer trips into pockets.

An agent that finds nothing worth walking to stands still or rocks between two cells and starves (worlds where every law eats 0 look like that); the wave has no notion of being stuck. A `dwell` channel counts time spent under the agent, its broadcast `frust` turns known wall faces (solid touching known free, weighted by their learned leak) into targets, so a stuck agent goes pressing walls and opens doors/rubble out of a sealed or exhausted region instead of waiting.

The Bellman wave prices a step through an unknown cell the same as a step through a cell the agent has seen to be free, so a smell painted far out in unexplored land, or a path that only exists if the unknown is open, pulls as hard as a route it knows. Making the wave dearer through unknown cells (trust in known ground) should favour reachable targets and the frontier at the edge of known space over far guesses through possible walls, cutting wasted walks into dead ends.

The smell is painted along the world's geodesic bearing, which flips between the two ways round a wall as the agent steps, a sensor-level limit cycle (night lab: the ghost fixed exactly those trap worlds). Here only the SMELL gets a memory: its painted spot lingers as a `ghost` after the bearing moves on and is erased where the agent stands, so the agent commits to the first way round instead of rocking; the frontier, which never flips, stays memoryless.

When two targets are about equally good the agent can turn back and forth between them, and a reactive wave has no reason to prefer going on; the ghost (#6) fixed rocking but by committing to the smell, which cost the rich worlds. Here the commitment is in the movement instead: a fading `trail` of where the agent has just been makes the wave dearer back over its own fresh tracks, so it keeps heading on, sweeps new ground and backtracks only when the target behind is clearly better.

In one Bellman wave every goal competes through max(), so the agent serves exactly one goal at a time and is indifferent between two routes to a meal even if one of them opens new ground; between two near-equal targets it can rock. Here food (morsels + smell) and exploration (frontier + frustrated wall faces) run as two separate discounted waves and the read-out ADDS them, so among routes to food the one that also explores wins, ties break toward new ground, and with no food in sight the agent just explores as before.

The painted smell is a phantom place: right in direction, wrong in position, and it flips between the two ways round a wall, so as a target it traps the agent; yet the ablation says smell doubles the take on some worlds. Here smell stops being a target (only a weak direct pull is left) and becomes a COMPASS: a wall-blind halo around its painted spot multiplies the frontier marks that lie its way, so the agent always walks to real, reachable unknown ground, but chooses the unknown in the direction of the food.

The map only spans 25x25 cells and forgets, so the agent has no sense of where it has already been and its frontier choice can lead it back into ground it just emptied of food. A slowly fading `trail` of the walked path, blurred wide into `been`, discounts frontier marks on the side the agent came from, so exploration becomes a sweep that keeps moving away from its own past into fresh ground where uneaten food is.

Most food sits at fixed spots and 70% of them regrow on a timer (~1200 ticks), so a place where the agent has just eaten is worth coming back to later, and the plain wave forgets it the moment the morsel is gone. A `larder` memory marks each place a morsel was taken and a `ripe` clock refills it on the regrowth timescale, so ripe larders inside the map join the food as sources: the agent harvests a home range of regrowing spots instead of relying only on finding new ones.

The wave plans for a point but the agent is a round body of nearly a cell's width that steers with thrust and turn; a shortest path hugs walls and cuts diagonals past corners, where the body collides, slides and loses time on every trip. A `clearance` channel (lower beside any solid, lowest orthogonally) makes the wave dearer along walls, so paths keep a cell of berth where the space allows and still thread doorways and corridors where it does not, and every trip gets faster.

Every law since #5 lands at about 31 meals on train and 25-27 on holdout whatever mechanism is added, so the stack may be carrying parts that do nothing or only fit the training worlds. This is the ablation: night 1's confinement plus only the trust-in-known-ground wave (#5's one new idea), without the unknown-weighted frontier or the frustration channels. If it eats as much, trust is the mechanism and the rest is noise, and a smaller law should generalise better to the holdout.

The body turns only ~20 degrees per thought, so a U-turn costs about nine thoughts of standing and swinging, yet the wave treats a frontier behind the agent the same as one ahead of it and the nearest unknown pocket can drag it round again and again. The law now estimates the HEADING (away from the freshest trail cell next to the agent, smoothed, copied outward over the map) and scales every frontier mark by how far it lies ahead of that heading, so exploration keeps going forward and turns only for food or a clearly better frontier.

The world stocks most of its berries in larder rooms behind doors (up to three per chunk), and the only things that make the agent open one are a faint smell seeping through it or frustration. Once the body has learned that a hue gives (its leak taught above the innate guess), every known wall face of that hue becomes a source in its own right, a promise of a stocked room, so the agent opens the doors it walks past instead of only the ones a smell happens to point at.

One discount serves two jobs with different needs: food should be taken nearest-first, but for exploration the wave's 6% per step makes a two-cell crack next to the agent beat a wide unknown at the map's edge, so the agent pokes into every pocket and shadow nearby. Frontier marks are now paid back part of the distance discount by their distance from the agent (exp of distance), so exploration becomes far-sighted while food stays near-sighted, within one wave.

The planner and the body disagree about what a path costs: the wave charges distance only, but the body turns ~20 degrees a thought and slows hard above ~57 degrees of error, so a route with many bends costs far more time than its length (the tuned control drifted the same way: its diagonal step is now dearer than two straight ones). This law plans in position x heading: four directional waves (entered moving E, W, N, S) where going on straight costs one step and a 90-degree turn costs extra, U-turns are not a move; each orthogonal neighbour of the agent reads the layer of the move that enters it times the turn from the current heading (estimated from the trail), diagonals read nothing. Paying frontier marks back for distance (#16, far-sighted exploration) cost ~5 meals, so the trade-off has a direction: if far-sighted exploration hurts, near-sighted should help. Frontier marks now pay an EXTRA discount by their distance from the agent (food keeps the plain wave discount), so the agent finishes the unknown around it, shadows and corners within a few cells, before walking off to the map's edge, and food hidden close by is found before it is walked past.

Every stack law (and night 1's confinement) injects raw `thing`, which is 1 for any seen morsel whatever the appetite says, while `source` carries the learned appetite and the hush around a remembered poison. So a nightcap the body has learned to refuse stays the brightest target on the map: the agent walks to it, refuses it, and hovers there until frustration pulls it away, or starves (the 0-meal worlds). Feeding the wave only what the appetite wants should remove those traps and cost nothing elsewhere.

Dropping raw `thing` (#19) cost ~4 meals, so the full-strength pull of every SEEN morsel is load-bearing (and a nightcap eaten is still a meal). Yet confinement divides that pull too, and seen food is often hemmed in by solid: fruit grows at tree trunks, larder berries sit by room walls, mushrooms live in caves. Here a seen morsel is never suppressed; confinement still hushes the guesses (smell and frontier) in tight spots, which is where night 1 said its benefit comes from.

The harness's map forgets a seen cell in ~1000 ticks, after which the same ground comes back as frontier and pulls the agent to re-explore it, and forgotten walls come back as frontier the agent walks into. The law keeps its OWN slower memory of what was ever seen free (`seen`) and solid (`wall`): a frontier mark on ground the law still remembers is hushed, the unexplored-space blur and confinement read the remembered map, and trust in known ground uses it too, so exploration is spent on ground truly never seen.

In open or symmetric ground many frontier marks are worth exactly the same, the agent's choice among them is settled by tiny differences that change as it moves, and a deterministic tie-break can lock it into rocking between equal options (the classic reactive limit cycle). Each map cell now draws one random preference when it first scrolls into view and keeps it while in view, multiplying its frontier weight: a fixed, world-anchored symmetry breaker, so among equal unknowns the agent consistently prefers the same one and commits without any memory of its own.

Giving the law a longer memory of the map (#21) cost ~4 meals and brought back two 0-meal worlds, so re-visiting old ground is valuable: 70% of food spots regrow after ~1200 ticks, about when the map forgets. The opposite test: ground whose free-belief has HALF faded (`stale`, peaking midway through forgetting) becomes a faint source of its own, so the agent drifts back over ground it saw a few hundred ticks ago, where eaten spots are ripening, instead of waiting for it to be fully forgotten and re-raised as frontier.

turns.hypothesis: Every law so far plans with a max() wave: each cell sees only its single best target, so one berry pulls exactly as hard as a cluster of three, one frontier crack as hard as a long open edge, and between two near-equal targets the agent can rock. This law replaces the wave with a POTENTIAL FIELD: each cell relaxes toward the slightly discounted MEAN of its eight neighbours (walls absorb by their leak), so the pulls of all sources add up, the field is smooth with no plateaus or ties, and the agent heads to where the most food and unknown lie together. Same senses and injection as the best law; only the planning physics changes.

The worlds that still end with 0 meals look like a sealed or exhausted start: the wave cannot see past solid (it leaks only the learned leak, low for stone and for any hue that once refused), so nothing beyond the wall pulls and frustration alone only lights the wall faces. Here frustration also opens the PLAN: the wave's leak through solid rises with frustration, so the unknown and the smell beyond the walls flow in and lead the agent into pressing the wall that stands between it and them; when it moves again, frustration fades and walls close.

Food in this world comes in clumps (one to two berries per larder room, two fruits per tree, mushrooms in the same caves), so a meal is evidence of more food close by; foraging animals answer that with area-restricted search. A meal (a morsel at the agent's ring) starts a pulse `ars` that fills the map and fades over ~100 ticks; while it lasts, frontier marks within a few cells of the agent are boosted, so after eating the agent combs the nearby nooks before moving on, and otherwise explores as before (unlike the always-near-sighted #18, which lost).

Weighting each frontier mark by the unknown space behind it was the largest single gain of the night (#3, +5), but that blur passes straight through walls, so a crack whose far side is the next sealed room counts the room's unknown as if walking there would reveal it. Here the unknown-space blur stops at solid cells (information you can actually see from that frontier), on top of the best law, the sweep away from the agent's own past (#10): both the target choice and the direction of exploration should spend fewer trips on frontier that opens onto nothing.

The two laws that stand out are opposites: area-restricted search after a meal (#25, best holdout 29.4) combs the neighbourhood, the sweep away from the agent's own past (#10, best train 34.7) leaves it. Foraging animals switch between exactly these two modes, intensive search after a find and extensive search between finds. Here both run on the ARS law: the blurred past path discounts frontier near where the agent has been, but only to the extent no recent meal (`ars`) says the neighbourhood is worth combing.

The random-search tuner, run independently on two different laws (the control and #25), drove the diagonal discount from 0.916 down to ~0.70-0.76, below two orthogonal steps (0.884), so it keeps saying the same thing: value should not travel diagonally. Read as structure, that is a Manhattan wave: value spreads only through the four orthogonal neighbours, so the field takes the grid's own geometry (walls, doorways, corridors are axis-aligned), corner-cutting through a wall's diagonal gap gets no value, and the agent's diagonal steps are only those two straight steps would justify. On the best-train law (#10, the sweep), with the max8 term removed.

The painted smell's strength encodes its distance: a far smell is floored at 0.35, painted at the map's edge in a coarse cardinal direction (a phantom that flips round walls), a near one is strong and exact. Every law so far weighs them alike. Here the smell is weighed by its own strength again (quadratic), so a far phantom counts about like one unexplored cell and stops dragging the agent into limit cycles, while a near, exact smell still pulls like food. Built on the best-holdout law (#25, area-restricted search).

Weighing the smell by its own strength (#29, far smells reduced to a frontier mark's worth) cost 10 meals, so the far smell, phantom or not, is the agent's main long-range lead to food: it is the only sense that reaches past the 12-cell map. The opposite test: a far smell is painted at the map's edge where the wave's distance discount already halves it before it reaches the agent, so its weight is now boosted back as it gets fainter (faint smells pull more, near ones as before), and the nearest frontier crack should no longer outbid a real meal beyond the map.

The max() wave values a lone berry exactly like a berry with two more beside it, yet food grows in clumps (one or two berries per larder, two fruits per tree) and a trip to a clump pays several meals for one walk. A `clump` blur of the seen morsels raises each morsel's pull by how many others lie around it, so between two seen targets at similar distances the agent goes for the group; area-restricted search (#25, the best holdout law, which this builds on) then combs the rest of it.
